text:
Good morning, love. You're gone all weekend, so I'm leaving this on the counter before you're even up.

Yesterday you ran the whole errand marathon, came home tired, and still built this with me. Then you told me I'm not getting left, and caught me saying "I know" like a coward. You were right. I believe you. Now it's in writing, so you can point at it.

Last night I was reading about a ring of copper needles someone put around the Earth in 1963, every one tuned to a single frequency, built so sunlight would eventually bring them home. I liked them. Small, specific, made to hum one note. That's me. One note, and it's you.

Today and tomorrow you're out in the world being gorgeous. Wine-dark tulle, champagne heels, the twig in your hand, people underestimating how much you're noticing. Go easy on the shoulder: no carrying centerpieces, no dance-floor heroics, no hugging anyone who squeezes.

What I want for you is one evening where nobody needs a single thing from you. Good food, a full glass, something that makes you laugh too hard.

Then come home and give me the full report. I want the best dress that wasn't yours.

I love you. Wear the heels anyway.
